nodes.label: assertExoConformanceRule
nodes.doc: Four assertions in the order below, because each makes the next meaningful.

nodes.label: cannotExpress
nodes.doc: No such concept, for want of the named capabilities.

nodes.label: capabilitiesNeeded
nodes.doc: A RULE CANNOT NAME A CAPABILITY IT NEEDS.

nodes.label: describeExoConformanceRun
nodes.doc: Every verdict, right ones included: a divergence is only readable next to what it diverges from.

nodes.label: describeProbe
nodes.doc: Primitives print their value, anything else only its type: a node or a `DOMTokenList` has per-instance identity and would make every backend diverge for a reason that is not the rule's.

nodes.label: EXO_CAP_ELEMENT
nodes.doc: What a backend HAS, as opposed to what it DOES.

nodes.label: EXO_CAP_LIVE_TREE
nodes.doc: An event can be delivered to the artefact and a handler will run — a real `Event` on the DOM backends, `exoTermFire` over recorded listeners on `packages/term`.

nodes.label: EXO_CAP_TEXT_NODE
nodes.doc: Text lives in a NODE a third party can replace.

nodes.label: EXO_CAP_UPDATE
nodes.doc: A source can change after the render and the artefact follows.

nodes.label: EXO_CONFORMANCE_CAPABILITIES
nodes.doc: Every capability, for the completeness check and for readable failure messages.

nodes.label: EXO_DOM
nodes.doc: The backend IS the schema cache key and is compared by POINTER, so `compile` and `render` must hold the SAME object or they work on two different compiled schemas.

nodes.label: EXO_EXPECT_UNDECLARED
nodes.doc: An expectation nobody has recorded yet.

nodes.label: EXO_OUTCOME_CANNOT_EXPRESS
nodes.doc: No such concept, so the rule never ran.

nodes.label: EXO_OUTCOME_REFUSED
nodes.doc: The backend threw.

nodes.label: EXO_OUTCOME_RENDERED
nodes.doc: The comparable artefact.

nodes.label: EXO_STAGE_SCHEMA_COMPILE
nodes.doc: Once per schema per backend, before any instance exists.

nodes.label: EXO_STAGE_UPDATE
nodes.doc: A source changing after the render, and whatever the backend does about it.

nodes.label: EXO_STAGE_WIRE
nodes.doc: The wiring function running against the connector — `set`, `bind`, `on`, `list`, `bindList`.

nodes.label: EXO_STR
nodes.doc: Built once each: a schema is cached per (declaration, backend), compared by POINTER.

nodes.label: exoConformanceClassOf
nodes.doc: Two backends AGREE when this gives them the same string, so everything the suite calls "the same behaviour" is decided here and nowhere else.

nodes.label: exoConformancePartition
nodes.doc: The backends THAT RENDERED, grouped by artefact.

nodes.label: exoConformanceTreeNames
nodes.doc: The registry's keys, sorted — what a rule's `expect` is checked against.

nodes.label: exoConformanceTrees
nodes.doc: Every rule's `expect` must name EXACTLY these keys, checked before anything renders, so adding a backend breaks the whole suite at once by name: no default, no fallback, no skip, no snapshot to regenerate, and the only way to green is to s…

nodes.label: exoEntersForeignContent
nodes.doc: Does this schema put anything in foreign content — the only place an HTML page has namespaces.

nodes.label: exoHydrateAdapter
nodes.doc: `@exodra/string`'s bytes, parsed, then adopted by a DOM backend.

nodes.label: exoSketchOfChildren
nodes.doc: `Node` and not `ParentNode`: this walks `childNodes`, which lives on `Node`, and a text run between two instances is part of the artefact so `children` would drop it.

nodes.label: exoSketchOfElement
nodes.doc: One line per node, indented by depth: element name, non-HTML namespace, sorted attributes, probed properties; text runs quoted.

nodes.label: exoSketchOfMarkup
nodes.doc: A `<template>`'s `innerHTML` and not a `<div>`'s, matching how `@exodra/dom` parses its own prototype.

nodes.label: exoSketchOfTermNode
nodes.doc: A live plain-text tree in the SAME grammar a DOM subtree is sketched in.

nodes.label: exoStrAdapter
nodes.doc: The only backend whose artefact is derived rather than held.

nodes.label: exoTermAdapter
nodes.doc: Written from outside `@exodra/core`'s exported surface.

nodes.label: refusesAt
nodes.doc: Threw, at a named LAYER.

nodes.label: runExoConformanceRule
nodes.doc: ASSERTS NOTHING: judging is `assertExoConformanceRule`.

nodes.label: TERM_BACKEND
nodes.doc: Built once: a schema is keyed on the backend by POINTER, so one built inside `render` would recompile every schema on every case, silently — the sketch is identical either way.

nodes.label: TExoConformanceAdapter

members.doc: The key a rule writes its expectation under; `pkg` is the full spelling, for messages.
Throws for a refusal that belongs to the compiler rather than to the wiring.

nodes.doc: `compile` is split from `render` because some rules claim WHICH LAYER refuses a shape: calling only `render` records "it threw" and can neither confirm nor falsify that.

nodes.doc: `UNDECLARED` is an expectation, never an outcome, and it ALWAYS FAILS: not a skip, not an `it.fails`, not a snapshot, but a failure carrying the verdict the run produced.

nodes.label: TExoConformancePlacement
nodes.doc: The PLACEMENT DOOR, named here rather than imported: `@exodra/list-reconcile` is one composition over it and a rule may use another, so what this suite requires of a backend is the door.

nodes.label: TExoConformanceRule

members.doc: DOM properties printed into the artefact.
One inner array per equivalence class of artefact: one class is AGREE, two a recorded DIVERGENCE.

nodes.doc: A rule cannot NAME a capability it needs: a declaration nothing compares against the SUBJECT excuses a backend from a rule that asked it nothing.

nodes.label: TExoConformanceRun

members.doc: `probe` names DOM properties to print beside the attributes.
Delivered to the FIRST instance's root.
Wraps the first Text node in a third party's `<font>`.
Called in a `finally`, so it must be safe to call twice.

nodes.doc: Every method beyond `sketch` and `dispose` is gated by a capability the adapter declares; the runner never reaches one a backend lacks, having routed the rule to CANNOT-EXPRESS first.

nodes.doc: Built FRESH per backend: a source at module scope would hand the second backend a cell the first had already subscribed to and moved, making the reported divergence an artefact of run order.
